correctness.rationale: Theorem A (inner disc) is fully rigorous and was independently replayed: tail majorant T(r,n)<=a/(1-q) with a=r^{n+1}/(n+1)!, q=r/(n+2) is valid since (n+2)...(n+j)>=(n+2)^{j-1} and q=0.25-0.2625<1 for 10<=n<=14; exp upper bound S30+b/(1-q) with q=r/32<1 bounds all-positive remainder; both computed in exact Fraction arithmetic. Re-ran inputs/artifacts/inner_cert.py: exact products T*U=0.11885,0.12652,0.13496,0.14422,0.15435<1, so |e^z-s_n|<=T<e^{-r}<=|e^z| on |z|=r=0.30n. Rouche then gives 0 zeros in |z|<r and none on |z|=r; e^z zero-free. Boundary strictness handled. Theorem B (outer circle) logic verified and replayed: L_n=R*sum_{k<n}R^k/k! exactly dominates max|s_n'| on |z|=R (s_n'=sum_{j<n}z^j/j!), so tube=L*Dt_up contains inter-node arcs; Machin pi upper bound via alternating Leibniz remainder (even M=8 upper, odd M=3 lower, terms decreasing for 0<x<1) is valid; per-segment check |c|_low>rho+sigma implies true-arc-to-polygon homotopy in C-minus-{0}; exact Fraction crossing-count winding is well-defined since homotopy keeps polygon away from 0. Re-ran outer_cert.py (N=16384): min|c|=64.31-950.40, node radii<=3.3e-08, tubes 4.04-120.7, worst (rho+sigma)/|c|_low=0.067-0.133 PASS everywhere, exact windings 10,11,12,13,14. Independently cross-checked Lipschitz dominance by dense sampling and root moduli via numpy.roots (n=10:3.64-6.56 ... n=14:4.77-9.53, strictly inside [0.30n,0.75n]). Outer rigor is conditional on documented IEEE-754 correct-rounding and <=8ulp libm assumptions, honestly disclosed as machine-checked certificate not formal proof; 7.5x margin makes silent unsoundness quantitatively implausible but not excluded. Proof vs evidence properly separated (Sec.4 numpy checks labelled evidence only). No essential inference, boundary condition, or computation fails.

originality.rationale: Substantive comparison, not timestamp: Enestrom-Kakeya for coefficients 1/k! gives ratios k+1, hence universal annulus 1<=|z|<=n; the claim strictly tightens both sides over 10<=n<=14 (inner 3.0-4.2 vs 1, outer 7.5-10.5 vs 10-14) and is not contained in EK. Newman-Rivlin (1972) Szego curve, Carpenter-Varga-Waldvogel (1991) scaled-zero asymptotics, and Saff-Varga (1976) parabolic zero-free regions are n->infinity limit-shape/descriptive results with no explicit finite-n disc/annulus enclosure; they imply no uniform 0.30n-0.75n certificate and their leftmost asymptotic |z|/n->W(1/e)~0.2785 is consistent with but does not imply the finite-n 0.30 bound. No listed reference contains a finite-degree Rouche-plus-interval enclosure for these n. Method is textbook components (Rouche + validated homotopy) but the specific uniform certificate with 6-7x margins and exact-rational inner proof is not a parameter substitution of any asymptotic theorem. Modest but genuine delta.

value.rationale: Independently worth finding later as a citable finite-degree lemma, not a textbook restatement or epsilon tweak: (i) inner radius changes qualitative scaling from EK constant 1 to linear 0.30n (3-4.2x gain), directly usable as stability-certificate lemma; (ii) outer radius cuts EK uniformly by exactly 25% over the window with >=7.5x certified margin; (iii) closed annulus is much thinner than EK and sharp within ~15% of true moduli (true min/n~0.34-0.36, max/n~0.66-0.68); (iv) motivated by Taylor time-stepping/Pade stability where moderate-degree explicit enclosures are the scarce resource, asymptotics give no finite-n certificate; (v) replayable in ~1s with stdlib only. Narrow window (5 integers) and non-optimality limit scope but do not reduce to unexplained enumeration: every n carries a proof certificate, not just a table.
